reviews.text: The film is an innocent love song to the movies and all its crazy quirks. The Hollywood dream lives on proudly in The Disaster Artist.
reviews.author: Benedict Seal

reviews.text: Disaster Artist is a one-joke movie, and that joke is a person, but it’s a very good joke abetted by a very good supporting cast (including Seth Rogen doing his spot-on thing) and the fringe period details...
reviews.author: Vadim Rizov

reviews.text: Capturing the same balance of admiration, mockery, and craft as Tim Burton's Ed Wood (1994), Franco's film pays homage to a cinematic rarity.
reviews.author: Brian Eggert

reviews.text: The Disaster Artist is nothing short of a beautiful disaster. A film that puts a spotlight on two men who shared a bond that led the greatest bad film of all time to be made.
reviews.author: David Gonzalez

reviews.text: It overflows with optimism and support for those who do whatever it takes to make their dreams come true.
reviews.author: Drew Dietsch

reviews.text: What's the inherent value of making a movie like this?
reviews.author: Fletcher Powell

reviews.text: One of the worst ever films is the subject of one of 2017's best.
reviews.author: Olly Richards

reviews.text: The new film is a love letter to the movies and how they are the stuff dreams are made of.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: Franco recreates The Room's hopeless ineptitude, with spot-on re-enactments of some of its most notoriously dire scenes. But the big surprise is that the decidedly odd, bromantic friendship at the movie's heart should prove so touching.
reviews.author: Jason Best

reviews.text: Whatever the real truth is, this ride is full of laughs.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: The Disaster Artist truly captures how the struggle for success shaped 'The Room,' the infamous disaster film we've come to love.
reviews.author: Leigh Monson

reviews.text: It's a film about the making of the film and the cult of personality that turned that otherwise disastrous film into an unexpected money maker.
reviews.author: Richard Propes

reviews.text: ...unfortunately, The Disaster Artist is also something of a vanity project for Franco, and a bit too much of an in-joke.
reviews.author: Joanne Laurier

reviews.text: It's not enough to glean any real insight, but it's just enough to entertain.
reviews.author: Matt Cipolla

reviews.text: The Disaster Artist is a fascinating character study of a delusional obsessive...it's not so much about the making of this cult film as it is about following your passions, no matter what, and accepting where that path leads you.
reviews.author: Damond Fudge

reviews.text: An oddball love letter to movies, a fascinating crowd-pleaser, and a surprisingly sweet story of passion and friendship.
reviews.author: Brent McKnight

reviews.text: [T]he decision to film Disaster as a comedy relegates the characters' moral objections to fodder for the funnies.
reviews.author: CJ Sheu

reviews.text: The audacity of Wiseau carries the film for a bit, but we never get his full background or how he got a cool 6 mill for such an inert, softcore bore.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: t's an underdog story that ultimately has the last laugh, given we're watching James Franco recreate Tommy's life for a film that has become the dark horse this awards season.
reviews.author: Dan Tabor

reviews.text: If you've never seen The Room, don't try to figure out the phenomenon; simply enjoy witnessing the [creation] of it. And if you are, in fact, a Room devotee, prepare to laugh harder than you have ever laughed in your life.
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: What it all amounts to is a tremendously funny feel good film that doesn't quite stand on its own so much as it plays as a great (the BEST, really) companion-piece to The Room that a cult film fan could ask for.
reviews.author: Dan Scully

reviews.text: The Disaster Artist is undeniably fun, but just skin deep.
reviews.author: Jorge Ignacio Castillo

reviews.text: Franco is all business portraying it's writer, director, producer and possible vampire and his strange behavior during the making of the movie. Oscar nomination for Franco? Better be. Oscar nomination for the movie? Possibly.
reviews.author: Shawn Edwards

reviews.text: By directing and acting in a movie about a bad actor/director, Franco the movie star made himself vulnerable -- and created the best film of his career.
reviews.author: Chris McCoy

reviews.text: This is one of the funniest movies ever made. James Franco should be nominated for an Oscar for his performance. The film is non-stop laughter, with a few serious moments. I loved it.
reviews.author: Sarah Knight Adamson

reviews.text: The Disaster Artist is unique, off kilter and strangely inspiring in the end. To his credit, it's a movie only a fellow wierdo like James Franco could make. Go see it.
reviews.author: Grethe Kemp

reviews.text: With this film, Tommy Wiseau has become famous again. He's selling Wiseau underwear and going on tour. He may be a Disaster Artist but with [James] Franco's help, he's having the last laugh.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: The Disaster Artist is lovely and savvy enough to find the genuine inspiration in such an unlikely yet true story.
reviews.author: Rhys Tarling

reviews.text: It is a fun and magical series that balances well its combination of comedy and drama while offering a delight to the viewer. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Víctor López G.

reviews.text: 'The Disaster Artist' is a great film that allows us to know a little better how such an unclassifiable work as 'The Room' was made. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mikel Zorrilla

reviews.text: Well-intentioned and sometimes genuinely funny but ultimately still a little depressing.
reviews.author: Rita Cannon

reviews.text: Even Room obsessives who have read the book multiple times should find themselves laughing anew; the material is gold, and and handled masterfully.
reviews.author: Oscar Goff

reviews.text: A lovingly made homage to a film so inconceivably created, it not only deepens the cultish reverie of the film but adds a certain textual dimension to the still resonant Hollywood dream of making it in show business.
reviews.author: Nicholas Bell

reviews.text: The spiritual companion piece to Ed Wood, The Disaster Artist is another cheerful Hollywood-insider piece about a man whose ambitions far outweigh his expertise.
reviews.author: Matt Brunson

reviews.text: A triumphant comedic companion to the 'The Room'.
reviews.author: Jeff Mitchell

reviews.text: So how is it? In a word, unnecessary. But in two words? Unnecessary and hilarious
reviews.author: D. Patrick Rodgers

reviews.text: One can't quite escape the feeling that it's punching down rather than up, its detached irony ending up as too arch and smug to really stick the landing.
reviews.author: Mattie Lucas

reviews.text: It's a complete portrait of the pitfalls and the rewards of being obsessively committed to want you want.
reviews.author: Dan Murrell

reviews.text: With The Disaster Artist James Franco has directed his most fun and honest movie. A real tragicomical achievement. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Nicolás Ruiz

reviews.text: It's no Ed Wood... but I was entertained.
reviews.author: Rachel Wagner

reviews.text: The director-producer-star's performance as notorious oddball Wiseau is nothing short of delightful, combining alien impetuousness, lopsided surrealist humour and a childlike sense of hope and wonder.
reviews.author: Rhys Handley

reviews.text: It's no surprise that "The Disaster Artist" is funny, but what is surprising is how moving it can be.
reviews.author: Allen Adams

reviews.text: I simply cannot endorse a film that excuses and glorifies the abusive behavior of a rich and powerful man with a victim complex.
reviews.author: Jourdain Searles

reviews.text: [The Disaster Artist] not only lovingly recreates so many of its trademark scenes, it is full of compassion for those who will never fit in.
reviews.author: Andrea Thompson

reviews.text: There is a perfect balance of humor mixed with drama that makes for a good time at the movies. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: David Ocadiz

reviews.text: By recreating the true story behind a weird film, Franco also creates a weird film.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: The finest film about Hollywood foibles since Ed Wood
reviews.author: Kyle Pinion

reviews.text: This absurdist comedy about an enigmatic auteur emerges as Franco's warmest, most crowd-pleasing directorial effort to date.
reviews.author: Andrew Wyatt

reviews.text: A total triumph, and thank goodness for that. Imagine if it had been terrible and someone else had to make a film about the making of the worst film ever made about the making of the worst film ever made. We'd be here for decades, getting ever more meta.
reviews.author: Sarah Cartland

reviews.text: A good movie about a bad cult classic that embodies the essence of Hollywood: dream big, stumble spectacularly, but never let your failures define you.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: This isn't the next coming of a great meta-masterpiece, but its largely a damn good retelling of one of Hollywood's most beautiful disasters.
reviews.author: James Clay

reviews.text: Never has a bad movie been so good - The Disaster Artist will delight members of the Tommy Wiseau cult and newcomers simultaneously.
reviews.author: Alistair Ryder

reviews.text: The genius of The Disaster Artist is that they made a universally funny movie that doesn't alienate anyone in the audience who hasn't seen The Room.
reviews.author: Kent Garrison

reviews.text: The Disaster Artist is more about circumstance and the unexpected virtues of vanity projects than it is about who the people at its center really are. It still comes off as a wildly entertaining ride -- and one I'd happily take again.
reviews.author: Tomas Trussow

reviews.text: The Disaster Artist finds James Franco and brother Dave Franco homaging the world's worst movie with one of their bests.
reviews.author: Matt Oakes

reviews.text: Eventually wants to posit the ironic enthusiasm of The Room's midnight-movie fandom as a kind of "validating moment" for Wiseau and company - in effect, congratulating its makers and stars for being fans of The Room.
reviews.author: Bob Chipman

reviews.text: The Room endures because there's nothing quite like it, and The Disaster Artist presents a delightful portrait of why the cult classic has absolutely no peers in the world of so-bad-it's-good cinema.
reviews.author: Sean Mulvihill

reviews.text: Leave it to one of the most notorious 'best worst movies' to inspire something so entertaining.
reviews.author: Johnny Gayzmonic

reviews.text: The film sticks the landing and provides a funny and sincere look at the making of The Room as well as the relationship between Wiseau and Sestero. But enough about that. Anyway, how's your sex lives?
reviews.author: Harris Dang

reviews.text: Franco could have easily just played Wiseau's eccentricities for laughs, but he sheds a little light on the man, making the audience care about him.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: What begins as something so unfathomably absurd and truly hilarious becomes a surprisingly moving portrait of one man's unwavering love of filmmaking.
reviews.author: Doug Jamieson

reviews.text: It is wildly funny and strange and captivating. And its shot-for-shot consistency underscore the seriousness of Franco's devotion to the project. It will probably very soon become a cult classic of its own.
reviews.author: John Hendrickson

reviews.text: After The Big Sick and Lady Bird, here is another remarkable tutorial for life delivered through the most outstanding of personalities and the most compact of films.
reviews.author: Nguyên Lê

reviews.text: The Disaster Artist causes so much pleasure it should be illegal in more conservative states.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: [Franco's] created a movie that craves the reaction Wiseau never wanted but received anyway.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: I loved every minute of this film...we go to the movies to see characters, and Tommy is a character, all right...
reviews.author: Lisa Nesselson

reviews.text: The Disaster Artist is a love letter to The Room. The painstaking recreations of certain shots are fascinating to watch. Be sure to stay through the credits.
reviews.author: Kimberly Pierce

reviews.text: The Room falls under the category of "so bad it's good." The Disaster Artist, directed by James Franco, looks to capture everything that went wrong, and a few things that miraculously went right.
reviews.author: Robert Daniels

reviews.text: More than a mere impersonation, Franco invests Wiseau with a naïve vulnerability that makes this potentially horrifying and definitely deluded would-be artist into a sympathetic human being desperate to share his art with the world.
reviews.author: Pat Padua

reviews.text: As a meta commentary on the misunderstood visionary, The Disaster Artist is a triumph. Yes, it's another of Franco's earnest forays, but this one works because it's so deeply personal.
reviews.author: Adam Epstein

reviews.text: With solid direction and great performances from himself and the rest of his cast, this cinematic love letter to the best-worst movie ever made is one of the best of the year.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: I was simply struck by how lucky one wealthy, self-centered maniac got by gaining so much notoriety for something so lame. I think he inadvertently expressed something so raw and naked that it becomes watchable on another level.
reviews.author: Asia Frey

reviews.text: Overstays its welcome, and overplays the notion that Wiseau, though a chump, represents the true spirit of Hollywood dreams, but plenty of amusing moments.
reviews.author: Alison Rowat

reviews.text: Along with being endlessly funny, this film is a singular look at the debilitating cycles of rejection, and the ways in which a life-long villain can look like a hero when peacocking in the right light.
reviews.author: Glenn Heath Jr.

reviews.text: It is a bit odd to have such warm and fuzzy feelings about a film based on The Room, but there is a certain degree of affection for it.
reviews.author: Deirdre Crimmins

reviews.text: [The Disaster Artist] brings heart to a side of Tommy Wiseau and his fellow filmmakers that is not talked about enough...
reviews.author: Avram Vargas

reviews.text: The result is one heck of a blast.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: Keeping the story structure familiar likely acts as a way for the film to stay grounded as it explores its weird subject and you see them coming clearly.
reviews.author: Joshua Rivera

reviews.text: The Room is wondrously mindless, whereas The Disaster Artist is just kind of dumb.
reviews.author: Rich Juzwiak

reviews.text: Like everything James Franco directs, The Disaster Artist is a work of appropriation art.
reviews.author: A.S. Hamrah

reviews.text: The Disaster Artist is an incredibly entertaining movie, and Franco delivers a rendition of Tommy Wiseau that is award worthy.
reviews.author: Indra Arriaga

reviews.text: ...an intelligent comedy. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Iván Belmont

reviews.text: If the point was to show that Waseau was weird, the creators of this film achieve that point. However, you also have to wonder about the self-indulgence exhibited by James Franco.
reviews.author: Helen Herimbi

reviews.text: Overall, 'The Disaster Artist' is a triumph through and through.
reviews.author: Jamal Grootboom

reviews.text: The Disaster Artist is a film absent of substantial dilemmas. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: William Venegas

reviews.text: It is difficult to stop laughing. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: María Fernanda Mugica

reviews.text: The Disaster Artist ends up being almost the best possible movie about the worst movie of all time. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: ...an entertaining comedy with striking drama. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos Díaz Reyes

reviews.text: [James Franco's] performance is, for long stretches, the most admirable of the film. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Daniel Krauze

reviews.text: Funnier than Ed Wood and costarring James' brother Dave Franco, it's the best buddy picture about bad filmmakers since Boogie Nights.
reviews.author: Tim Appelo

reviews.text: The Franco brothers bring the same creative energy to their project that motivated Wiseau in his own endeavor. The difference is, they have talent.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: James Franco did a great job directing and starring in the movie...you appreciate the general mannerisms he has. He's not Daniel Day-Lewis, but he did a really good job.
reviews.author: Jeremy Jahns

reviews.text: As an actor, Franco effectively appropriated the tics of the one-man-orchestra Wiseau, but the comedy ends on the side of condescension and the punishment of others. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ernesto Diezmartinez

reviews.text: The story of Greg Sestero and Tommy Wiseau is quite special, and I don't regret experiencing it --at all-- either in book form, or through this excellent film. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: Perfectly balances eccentricity, humor and respect. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sergio López Aguirre

reviews.text: Extremely entertaining. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jonathan Sánchez

reviews.text: A satirical look at bad filmmaking that is itself bad filmmaking. . .Wiseau and Sestero are both pitied and ridiculed. . .The Disaster Artist is being bizarrely acclaimed, proof that the idea of art has died in Hollywood.
reviews.author: Armond White

reviews.text: A desperate love letter to cinema that puts the stupidity and nonsense of many of our dreams right before our eyes. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Roger Salvans

reviews.text: The Disaster Artist is a comedy that is frequently laugh-out-loud funny. But it is also sympathetic towards Wiseau's insatiable desire to create, to find fame.
reviews.author: James Marsh

reviews.text: There's a clear fondness for the subject matter here, a respect for the protagonists that goes beyond caricature, and an unexpected poignancy to the challenges.
reviews.author: Chris Newbould

reviews.text: This is the kind of stranger-than-fiction gold that gets crazier the deeper you delve into it.
reviews.author: Marwa Hamad

reviews.text: James Franco brings out a moving 'bromance' from 'The Room' while celebrating the creative impulse over talent. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Daniel de Partearroyo

reviews.text: ...large swaths of The Disaster Artist completely fail to completely capture and sustain one's interest...
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: The Disaster Artist unfortunately takes Wiseau as seriously as he took himself during the filming of The Room, but at least it provides some insight as to why the "worst movie" ever made was created.
reviews.author: Alachia Queen

reviews.text: The built-in level of affection and support between the two siblings lends the movie an extra layer of heart that helps keep The Disaster Artist from being the condescending hatchet job it could have become in many other directors' hands.
reviews.author: Carl Kozlowski

reviews.text: The result is one of the best comedies of the year. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Benjamín Harguindey

reviews.text: The Disaster Artist is arguably the most unlikely film about film-making in recent memory...resulting in one of the best comedies of the year.
reviews.author: Christopher Machell

reviews.text: The Disaster Artist might just usher in the golden era of Tommy Wiseau. Naaht a bad film at all.
reviews.author: Toby Woollaston

reviews.text: It's a hilarious and at times heartwarming film about the lengths people will go to achieve their wildest dreams.
reviews.author: Marlow Stern

reviews.text: This is the year's funniest film. I suspect that the more you know about how films are really made, the funnier this film will seem to you, and vice versa.
reviews.author: Robert Roten

reviews.text: A thoughtful, deeply humorous portrait of a man who wanted to make a movie in spite of the cynicism of others, and did so entirely on his terms - in this case, for far worse results than most.
reviews.author: David Keyes

reviews.text: A very trivial and insubstantial character study.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: Franco feels the same affection and respect for Tommy that the tandem Tim Burton/Johnny Depp have for Ed Wood. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: The film alternates between embracing the individual viewer and the collective appreciation of bad, bad art, and while we are often laughing uproariously at the audacity of the story unfolding, there are moments of sadness where we fear we shouldn't.
reviews.author: Brooke Corso

reviews.text: Anger and self-pity practically bleed off the screen in The Room, but The Disaster Artist only hints at what could have inspired such animus.
reviews.author: Margot Harrison

reviews.text: The movie condenses the complicated Wiseau-Sestero relationship into a broad "two friends take on Hollywood" narrative, robbing the story of so many of its eccentricities.
reviews.author: J. Olson

reviews.text: Oxymoronic, Oscar-quality acting that's simultaneously godawful!
reviews.author: Kam Williams

reviews.text: The success of The Disaster Artist is less a thoughtful almost-adaptation and more a testament to one man and his quest for greatness - even if it means being the worst of the best.
reviews.author: Jerilyn Jordan

reviews.text: It feels unhealthily backward-looking to allow Franco to elevate Wiseau to a hero worth rooting for.
reviews.author: Drew Grant

reviews.text: Even viewers who haven't see The Room should be able to relate to this affectionate real-life shaggy-dog tale about dreamers, set in the shadow of Hollywood.
reviews.author: Al Hoff

reviews.text: The fiercely clever casting alone makes it worth the price of admission, but this is also the kind of movie that makes us fall in in love with cinema all over again. And it'll make you less afraid to admit your guilty pleasures.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: James Franco has made a wickedly funny and very good movie from the ruins of one of the worst ever made.
reviews.author: Pete Hammond

reviews.text: It doesn't matter if you've seen The Room or not. You'll be laughing regardless at this truth is stranger than fiction tale.
reviews.author: Matthew Toomey

reviews.text: Instead of being consistently funny, much of the film is downright cringeworthy. As a cautionary tale, "The Disaster Artist" succeeds, but as a comedy, it's more disturbing and subversive than a laugh riot.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: When Franco and Rogen show up in something together, good things tend to happen.
reviews.author: Bob Grimm

reviews.text: Stacking the cast with a This is the End-style comedy ensemble, only to have them sit around commenting on Wisseau's follies like they were guests on a podcast, exposes the smugness at the movie's core.
reviews.author: Daniel Barnes

reviews.text: A wild true story about obsessively chasing a dream, finding a friend and yearning to belong, this Ed Wood-style effort will make you want to hurl spoons at the screen with sheer joy.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: Franco's film is disappointing and more than a little patronizing.
reviews.author: Carrie Rickey

reviews.text: The Disaster Artist is directed by James Franco, who also stars as Wiseau in a performance of fascinating weirdness.
reviews.author: Lisa Jensen

reviews.text: Please savor the irony that one of the worst movies ever made has inspired one of the best movies of 2017.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: As I laughed at The Disaster Artist, there's still a hint of sourness to the proceedings that made me feel crappy afterwards.It's easy to see that everyone involved has great affection for The Room, but I'm not sure that love carries over to Wiseau.
reviews.author: Jared Rasic

reviews.text: Here's an enjoyable account of the daffy behind-the-scenes goings-on during the filming of the cult film 'The Room.'
reviews.author: Linda Cook

reviews.text: As with Ed Wood, which paid tribute to the director of Plan 9 From Outer Space - another film that does not deserve its reputation as one of the worst ever made - The Disaster Artist champions the value of persistence in the face of all odds.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: We may never know exactly what was going on in Tommy Wiseau's mind when he created one of the worst movies ever made, but The Disaster Artist is a valiant attempt at understanding just that.
reviews.author: David Fontana

reviews.text: Franco leaves flattery behind and finds the authenticity of this man, pointing the way to a real shot at critical redemption for Wiseau and The Room.
reviews.author: tt stern-enzi

reviews.text: It's entertaining, if framed and cut a touch manically.
reviews.author: Ryan Gilbey

reviews.text: The irony is that this farcical comedy just might win the Oscar Wiseau always coveted. I'm sure Wiseau will take credit for it if it happens. And we won't mind.
reviews.author: Tim Martain

reviews.text: James Franco and the entire Disaster Artist team have created a modern fable. Someone who went for their dream achieved it in the most unlikely way possible. We can all relate.
reviews.author: Chris Gore

reviews.text: That sunnier-than-truth finale suits The Disaster Artist's relentlessly cockeyed optimism. Franco doesn't ask viewers to reconsider bad art but to respect the artist behind it.
reviews.author: Steve Persall

reviews.text: Although the humour is Marmite, the story is good.
reviews.author: Aine O'Connor

reviews.text: Franco's portrayal of him is brilliant: obscured by prosthetics and that impenetrable accent, he digs deep into Tommy's complex and by no means unsympathetic personality, and never makes the mistake of letting his character in on the joke.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: The film is still just an ironist freak show, albeit one now enacted by Franco and his celebrity friends.
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: Funny -- sometimes brutally -- and surprisingly touching, it works whether you've seen the source material or not, though there are plentiful shout-outs to die-hard fans.
reviews.author: Sara Stewart

reviews.text: The Disaster Artist is an endearing tale of friendship and chasing your dreams that packs a surprisingly poignant punch.
reviews.author: Chris Agar

reviews.text: The funniest bad movie ever made becomes a mildly amusing celebrity piss take with a few moments of shoe-horned conflict and plastic pathos.
reviews.author: Ed Whitfield

reviews.text: Director and star James Franco simply gets how to make a good film in equal measure to the ineptitude of Tommy Wiseau, whose classically bad movie becomes the subject of this very funny one.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: James Franco -- as we've never seen him before -- steals the show playing Tommy Wiseau in 'The Disaster Artist,' based on a true story.
reviews.author: Betty Jo Tucker

reviews.text: Good news, everyone: We found the role that James Franco was born to play.
reviews.author: Kristian M. Lin

reviews.text: Not "only" a good movie within a movie. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Quim Casas

reviews.text: Unlike its bosom buddy, Tim Burton's Ed Wood, it might be too niche a subject to resonate with mass audiences but it's evident Franco and crew are having a whale of a time.
reviews.author: Kristen Lopez

reviews.text: What do 'The Room' and The Disaster Artist have in common? An absolute dearth of insincerity.
reviews.author: Christian Toto

reviews.text: What distinguishes The Disaster Artist is that it celebrates drive and, much like an episode of American Pickers, turns trash into treasure.
reviews.author: Christopher Lawrence

reviews.text: Franco's performance as Wiseau is an extreme, frightening, hair-tearingly bizarre and almost always hilarious feat of daring.
reviews.author: David 'Mad Dog' Bradley

reviews.text: Franco clearly has a whale of a time with Wiseau's punch-drunk accent, bizarre mannerisms and dada laugh; it's a staggering piece of mimicry.
reviews.author: Jamie Dunn

reviews.text: The Disaster Artist proves through its onslaught of ludicrous scenarios, that truth can sometimes be much stranger than fiction.
reviews.author: Gemma Creagh

reviews.text: Perhaps this one is just for the die-hard fans, burning to know how such a bad film was ever brought to life. Clearly, I'm not one of them.
reviews.author: Keeva Stratton

reviews.text: Wiseau also makes a pretty good avatar for Franco himself: a mercurial, relentless performer whose ambition encompasses a thrilling willingness to crash and burn. And it's that identification that makes the comedy work here: Franco kids because he loves.
reviews.author: Matthew Lickona

reviews.text: Taking a cue from Ed Wood, this loving portrait of a terrible filmmaker could have indulged in ridicule, but instead it's about passion and dedication.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: Why The Disaster Artist works so well is that it doesn't judge our reactions to it; the film is not in the slightest ironic or, as is fashionable these days, meta.
reviews.author: Kirk Baird

reviews.text: "The Disaster Artist," James Franco's charming love letter to one of the most fabulously awful movies ever, earns "Hi Marks," indeed.
reviews.author: Maria Sciullo

reviews.text: I don't know if The Disaster Artist will rock your world, but I do know that I laughed at the comic touches that Franco, who also directed, brings to the subject of dismal failure.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: The Disaster Artist will remind of The Producers in places but there is another great movie that it also brings to mind - in Hollywood terms, it is the equivalent of This is Spinal Tap.
reviews.author: Alan Corr

reviews.text: "The Disaster Artist," despite all its Hollywood cynicism, has quite a big heart.
reviews.author: Michael Heaton

reviews.text: Seth Rogen steals the show as Sandy Schklair, a continuity expert who seems to be the only person involved with The Room who knows how a set or even real life works.
reviews.author: Piers Marchant

reviews.text: It's difficult to cheer on Wiseau as an anti-hero when it's not clear exactly what, other than a vehicle for his own narcissism, he was championing.
reviews.author: Rubin Safaya

reviews.text: The Disaster Artist is an enormously entertaining look at film making dreams and the legacy that comes with making a truly terrible one.
reviews.author: Bill Clark

reviews.text: Like Tim Burton's "Ed Wood," "The Room" is both a movie that pokes fun at its subject and celebrates it, with an odd but strangely inspiring message: Do what you love. Even if you're terrible at it.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: "The Disaster Artist" is a sweet, emotionally engaging tribute to friendship, the movies and the importance of dreams.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: James Franco's story about filmmaker Tommy Wiseau, his friendship with aspiring actor Greg Sestero and Wiseau's making of his film, "The Room," is funny, creepy and a most singular experience.
reviews.author: Bob Bloom

reviews.text: Wiseau, The Room and the making of a celluloid catastrophe are the subjects of The Disaster Artist, a fabulous, strange and frequently hilarious comedy-drama from the self-styled polymath James Franco.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: Some familiarity with "The Room" certainly enhances the humor here, but "The Disaster Artist" delivers its own inspired, often hysterical comedy.
reviews.author: Diane Carson

reviews.text: It's a benign salute to a midnight melodrama.
reviews.author: Richard von Busack

reviews.text: As with Ed Wood, its nearest cinematic neighbour, you don't need to have seen its subject's work to get the surprisingly sweet-toned humour that comes mostly at a pseudo-auteur's expense.
reviews.author: Ken Eisner

reviews.text: It might not be as amusing as discovering the mind-boggling awfulness of The Room for the first time, but it's a decent intro to the madness.
reviews.author: Josh Bell

reviews.text: If you strip the fiddly premise out, this is an immensely silly movie about an immensely silly person. Watch it. You'll be glad you did.
reviews.author: Lili Loofbourow

reviews.text: It's smart and funny and knowing, and is propelled by a strong cast led by Franco himself and his brother Dave.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: [The Disaster Artist] will surprise you at exactly the moment you think you've got it figured out.
reviews.author: Tara Thorne

reviews.text: The key to The Disaster Artist and Franco's success: he finds the heart and soul of the film. It's not difficult to predict what those things are, ultimately, but there will be no spoilers here. Go see it.
reviews.author: George M. Thomas

reviews.text: While it doesn't match the brilliance of 'Ed Wood,' it's a mightily enjoyable, and equally affectionate, tribute to a misguided moviemaker.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: If The Room is the "Citizen Kane of bad movies," as it has notoriously been tagged, then The Disaster Artist, the story of the making of that film, is the shaggy-dog redemption story that it deserves.
reviews.author: Michael Smith

reviews.text: Disaster Artist is... a consistently funny film that has enough warmth to make it an ode to both friendship and the artistic spirit, in whatever direction they may take.
reviews.author: Brad Keefe

reviews.text: The Disaster Artist should definitely first be seen in the theater, with a raucous crowd roaring with laughter. But later it should be seen at home where you can also observe the film's sneaky empathy and grace.
reviews.author: Max Weiss

reviews.text: I can't fault Franco and his collaborators for feeling affection for Wiseau, who after all has given so much joy to so many people, if only by accident.
reviews.author: M. Faust

reviews.text: Franco delivers a comedy that's delightfully offbeat. It probably helps if you've actually seen "The Room," but you can safely spare yourself that experience.
reviews.author: Calvin Wilson

reviews.text: Like Tim Burton's classic "Ed Wood," "The Disaster Artist" is a testament to the communal joy of movie-making. But more than that, it's an unforgettable appreciation of the pleasures of movie-watching.
reviews.author: Christopher Schobert

reviews.text: Both The Room and The Disaster Artist prove exceptions to the old adage that you can't polish a turd: while Wiseau saw his 'disasterpiece' evolve beyond his imagining, Franco, for his part, has spun tragicomic gold from the most tragic of base materials.
reviews.author: Matthew Taylor

reviews.text: [James] Franco has not just made a really sharp, funny movie about movie making. He's also made a layered and intimate portrait of a friendship with his own brother, Dave Franco.
reviews.author: Bob Mondello

reviews.text: "The Disaster Artist" is a lot of fun, even if some of it is uncomfortable. And of course it's way better than "The Room."
reviews.author: Bill Goodykoontz

reviews.text: This movie isn't just some Hollywood parody or inside joke. It takes Wiseau's humanity seriously and portrays him as a wounded individual who wanted to be an All-American James Dean-type hero and not the ogre or villain everyone else saw him as.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: Sincere and sporadically funny, The Disaster Artist is an endearing tribute to failing in Hollywood. Anyway, how is your sex life?
reviews.author: John Nugent

reviews.text: It's The Room with a view from people with talent, sniggering with a veneer of generosity to save face.
reviews.author: Tim Robey

reviews.text: It'd be an absolute tragedy if it wasn't so funny...
reviews.author: Travis Johnson

reviews.text: Funny and alarmingly factual.
reviews.author: Gary Thompson

reviews.text: A fascinating glimpse into the genesis of one of Hollywood's worst releases and is worthy of a space alongside Ed Wood on the shelf for dreamers who succeeded because of a lack of self-awareness and an epic void of talent.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: ... it is the enduring, infectiously unsettling weirdness of Tommy Wiseau which ultimately delivers one of the most amusing comedies of 2017.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: Like the hilariously inept melodrama of The Room itself, Tommy Wiseau offers Franco a gold mine of oddities.
reviews.author: Peter Canavese

reviews.text: "The Room," a movie that had audiences laughing AT the director is transformed into a laugh-out-loud film that has us laughing WITH the director.
reviews.author: Harvey S. Karten

reviews.text: Superficially slick, yet schlocky, a muddled misadventure...
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: Don't expect much new information to come to light if you've already read Sestero's book on which the film was based, though; despite a bravura performance from James Franco, Wiseau remains as inscrutable as ever.
reviews.author: Thaddeus McCollum

reviews.text: The side-by-side comparisons during the ending credits will leave you speechless if you're magically not already dead from laughing
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: Imbued with his own divisive but wholly vivid personal mythology, James Franco is just as important character to The Disaster Artist as Tommy is.
reviews.author: Michael Arbeiter

reviews.text: A good, shallow movie about a bad, shallow movie... Funny and highly energized.
reviews.author: Eric D. Snider

reviews.text: A hilarious ode to talentless passion. James Franco gives the bizarre Tommy Wiseau depth without solving his mystery, but skips a deserved zing at Hollywood.
reviews.author: MaryAnn Johanson

reviews.text: Franco gets credit for focusing every bit as much on the artist as the disaster - and for taking something most saw as trash and spinning it into something close to treasure.
reviews.author: Mike Scott

reviews.text: Franco plays this fascinating outsider with a cheeky wink, making for a very funny character study of a man who marched to the beat of his own drum.
reviews.author: Katherine McLaughlin

reviews.text: James Franco shows less conviction than his muse, Tommy Wiseau.
reviews.author: Josh Larsen

reviews.text: Even if you've never heard of The Room, what James Franco has to offer here a fantastic, hilarious true Hollywood story that is as phenomenal as its subject matter is awful.
reviews.author: Eric Eisenberg

reviews.text: James Franco's all-over-the-place career hits its sweet spot with his hugely entertaining recreation of one Hollywood hopeful's master class in how not to make a movie.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: The comedy, for all its scenes of giddy wonder, never gets past Tommy's mask of mystery; avoiding speculation and investigation, it stays on the surface of his public and private shtick, leaving little more than a trail of amusing anecdotes.
reviews.author: Richard Brody

reviews.text: The most surprising aspect about this singular movie about a singular individual is its universal entertainment value.
reviews.author: Vicky Roach

reviews.text: A great film and one of the must-sees for award season.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Lyles

reviews.text: The Disaster Artist is an indulgent salute to the cockeyed dreamers of the film world and softens its ridicule with a good measure of affection.
reviews.author: Allan Hunter

reviews.text: This is a film with heart as well as humour.
reviews.author: Andy Lea

reviews.text: James Franco hits all the right wrong notes in this hugely entertaining, true-life tale of Tommy Wiseau's 2003 "disasterpiece" film The Room.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: Tommy Wiseau is flat-out weird, even a tad scary, but Franco seldom fails to make his character's acute form of self-delusion charming and infectious.
reviews.author: Al Alexander

reviews.text: Sorry, must disagree with majority. This film is a frequently too boring film about boorish filmmaker with a lot of mystery money, Maybe as a five minute SNL skit. But as a feature, it's a drag.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: Hilarious... the film may be the best use to date of James Franco's off-kilter energy
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: The Disaster Artist is a study in empathy and this year's darker, grittier answer to La La Land, peddling as it does in the dreams of Angeleno artists.
reviews.author: Annlee Ellingson

reviews.text: The Disaster Artist has all the fascination of a train wreck and will be essential viewing for anyone at all interested in the current status of the film industry.
reviews.author: David Stratton

reviews.text: Fans of The Room will find much to love here, but even if you've never heard of it, The Disaster Artist should delight.
reviews.author: David Sims

reviews.text: It's a professional and personal triumph for the reinvigorated Franco.
reviews.author: Stephen Rebello

reviews.text: The Disaster Artist misses its shot at greatness but it is still an enormously entertaining work that serves as a celebration of the artistic process.
reviews.author: Peter Sobczynski

reviews.text: Even more impressively, Franco makes Wiseau, maybe the most unpleasant character he's ever played, someone you genuinely root for in his demented quest for greatness.
reviews.author: Dana Stevens

reviews.text: As a filmmaker, Franco has often tended toward high or performance art... The Disaster Artist allows for both these Francos to shine.
reviews.author: Tara Brady

reviews.text: By channeling his inner Tommy Wiseau, James Franco manages to craft an intentional comedic sensation out of an unintentionally hilarious failure, The Disaster Artist rising to a level of genuine greatness that's astonishing.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: Entertaining enough but increasingly repetitive as it goes. (Full Content Review for Parents - Profanity, Nudity, etc. - also Available)
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: Franco creates this heightened reality, almost like you've stepped into Bizarro World, where you're cheering for Tommy's movie to be as terrible as it possibly can be.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: A broad, winning adaptation of a fantastic book.
reviews.author: Vincent Mancini

reviews.text: Perhaps the greatest compliment one can pay Franco's The Disaster Artist is that it encourages audiences to laugh with Wiseau and his clueless cohorts rather than mock them.
reviews.author: J.R. Kinnard

reviews.text: When I saw the end of this bizarre movie, I realized that I enjoyed it more than I thought I had. The additional few scenes shown after fade-out are pretty amazing and eye-opening. In fact it was those scenes that raised my rating considerably.
reviews.author: Tony Medley

reviews.text: Franco transforms Sestero's BTS memoir into a genuinely touching tale of two outsiders.
reviews.author: Jacob Knight

reviews.text: The point is well taken - that both projects unapologetically deserve a place in the cinematic landscape, quality be damned.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: I can certainly imagine a director emerging from a screening of The Room filled with the fear that he's been making the same kind of movie this whole time. Maybe it just took a terrible movie to finally inspire James Franco to direct a good one.
reviews.author: Rain Jokinen

reviews.text: The Disaster Artist is a movie that supplements an excellent film and an entertaining book while not quite hitting either's mark, but it is entertaining.
reviews.author: Alex Doenau

reviews.text: A galaxy of great guest stars adds comic coats of appalled disbelief as Tommy makes his movie every wrong way he possibly can - while Franco, off-camera, makes one of the weirdest and best films about a movie ever.
reviews.author: Bob Strauss

reviews.text: It's also a reminder that Franco is a smart and funny performer with perverse comedic instincts that pay off constantly.
reviews.author: Sean Nelson

reviews.text: By the end of The Disaster Artist, Wiseau is still a joke.
reviews.author: Nick Allen

reviews.text: Like watching a meme come to life.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: Not a lot unlike watching The Room itself...
reviews.author: Kurt Loder

reviews.text: Franco's very funny movie meticulously re-creates The Room's most famously botched scenes, but shies away from its tortured soul.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: Funny, heartfelt and utterly bizarre.
reviews.author: Hannah Strong

reviews.text: Franco gives Wiseau and his story the film he was not able to give himself.
reviews.author: Nell Minow

reviews.text: It's one of the best, touching and funniest films you'll see this year - Franco will have some way to go before he can top this one.
reviews.author: Jamie East

reviews.text: On its own terms, The Disaster Artist is a funny movie.
reviews.author: Paul Byrnes

reviews.text: On one level it functions as a useful demolition job on the artist-as-savant myth that too many films and documentaries indulge, but on another it's a reminder that even bad art can spring from and inspire compelling human stories.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: Without the endorsement of real life, The Disaster Artist would tell a story far too weird to believe.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: So, to see the machinations behind it - the never-ending takes, the adding of the water bottle, Wiseau's commitment to "real human behavior" - gives depth to what, on the surface, appears purely trash.
reviews.author: Anne Cohen

reviews.text: Franco follows the model of Tim Burton's biopic Ed Wood, approaching Wiseau with a delicate balance of affectionate mockery and a heartfelt appreciation for his creative passion.
reviews.author: Scott Tobias

reviews.text: The old alchemist's trick of turning lead into gold has nothing on The Disaster Artist, a film that masters the trickier feat of transforming trash into art.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: There's something joyful about the Franco brothers playing a fun-house mirror version of their own Hollywood arrival, and the film's best scenes are with Rogen's production manager, aghast at Tommy's incompetence.
reviews.author: Jake Coyle

reviews.text: The film is ... funny -- hilarious at points -- and an enlightening look at the production of one of the most infamous movies ever made.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: Behind the camera is really where Franco flourishes, as there's a pace to "The Disaster Artist" that makes up it for its occasionally uneven and clunky structure.
reviews.author: Gregory Wakeman

reviews.text: Mr. Franco recreates the production of "The Room" - and the escalating behind-the-scenes nuttiness - with an assured, energetic touch ...
reviews.author: Manohla Dargis

reviews.text: Spelling out a joke may be the quickest way to kill it, but the obvious, expository nature of the mockery in "The Disaster Artist" doesn't make it any less funny or illuminating.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: The Disaster Artist is a truly, profoundly funny film. But it is also something more. There's a poignancy here and an insight into the necessary self-delusion that it takes to even imagine becoming a successful actor or film-maker.
reviews.author: Graeme Tuckett

reviews.text: It's a film to see with an audience familiar with what it's about to see, with people who can appreciate the dedication with which Franco and co. have recreated so many of the original film's woeful scenes and performances.
reviews.author: Jim Vorel

reviews.text: There's a nagging feeling we should expect something more from this guy. To borrow the most quotable line of dialogue from The Room (bellowed at the top of the lungs): "YOU ARE TEARING ME APART, FRANCO!"
reviews.author: Steve Davis

reviews.text: In a kooky yet vulnerable and heartfelt performance, Franco gets right at the heart of what makes Wiseau a true hero - his sheer willingness to try - and that is what makes "The Disaster Artist" work so well.
reviews.author: Katie Walsh

reviews.text: "The Disaster Artist" is a breezy, entertaining and even affectionate movie about the making of "The Room."
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: Perhaps Franco's two decades of résumé mongering has all along been in the service of harnessing the real freak he had inside all along.
reviews.author: Christian Lorentzen

reviews.text: Both the book and the movie try to explain what makes The Room such a phenomenon, but Franco loses patience and takes a scalpel to the story.
reviews.author: Steve Heisler

reviews.text: James Franco's very funny The Disaster Artist is possibly the best narrative film about an outsider filmmaker since Tim Burton's Ed Wood, and it's anchored by three wise choices.
reviews.author: Sherilyn Connelly

reviews.text: Given his own failed attempts at becoming an auteur, it is all too perfect that James Franco finally finds his muse, successfully humanizing one of cinema's few genuine eccentrics.
reviews.author: Alan Zilberman

reviews.text: The real genius of The Disaster Artist is its understanding of anti-genius.
reviews.author: K. Austin Collins

reviews.text: The Disaster Artist is still approximately 783 times better than the film it's lampooning. Intoxicating fun, it deserves to be on a double bill with The Room whenever the so-called 'Citizen Kane of bad movies' is shown.
reviews.author: Nicholas Barber

reviews.text: (James Franco's) team did a terrific job with the re-creation, and The Disaster Artist is a fun look at Hollywood dreams at their woolliest.
reviews.author: Joe Gross

reviews.text: In the end, "The Disaster Artist" decides that the only bad movies are the ones that fail to bring us joy. "The Room" certainly can't be accused of that.
reviews.author: Rafer Guzman

reviews.text: Should newcomers to this particular cinematic phenomenon see "The Room" first? Yes. Seeing "The Disaster Artist" is less crucial to their camp education.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: It's based on a true story, but you will shake your head in disbelief - in a good way.
reviews.author: Maren Longbella

reviews.text: Director/star James Franco allows us to laugh at Wiseau's atrocious acting, incomprehensible direction and oddball vanity but also encourages us to respect his creative spirit.
reviews.author: Larushka Ivan-Zadeh

reviews.text: [An] entertaining, if weirdly incurious and incomplete true-life story.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: As an artist, Wiseau was a disaster. But what a mess he made.
reviews.author: Leah Greenblatt

reviews.text: James Franco's film is a triumphant and uproarious comedy that celebrates flawed creators and their mistaken creations.
reviews.author: Rob Dean

reviews.text: Perhaps the biggest surprise about The Disaster Artist is how utterly sweet it is.
reviews.author: Jim Slotek

reviews.text: A terrific film about a terrifically terrible one, The Disaster Artist is good-bad movie gold. Double bill alert!
reviews.author: Matt Glasby

reviews.text: "The Disaster Artist" is a love letter to a freak, straddling the line between admiring and appalled.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: This sweet, affectionate (and unapologetically slight) comedy is an all-too-rare homage to harmless, hilarious incompetence, at a time when there is plenty of the more hurtful kind to go around.
reviews.author: Michael O'Sullivan

reviews.text: One of the funniest films I've seen in years ... epic chops as a faithful adaptation of an intriguing memoir, an odd-couple buddy movie, Tale of Hollywood, and meditation on ambition ... an honestly motivated biographical adaptation, not a piss-take.
reviews.author: CJ Johnson

reviews.text: The Disaster Artist -- James Franco's hyphenated turn as star, producer and director -- deftly falls into that comedic pantheon, joining the likes of Ed Wood in making an entertaining movie about a truly terrible one.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: The Disaster Artist is funny from the beginning, but it becomes downright side-splitting once Tommy gets onto a film set.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: What Franco's performance brings out is a sense of emotional pain that's perhaps not obvious in the real Tommy Wiseau.
reviews.author: Jason Di Rosso

reviews.text: It's a nice irony that one of the worst movies in recent history has enabled James Franco to make one of the best films in his own chequered career.
reviews.author: Geoffrey Macnab

reviews.text: For something based around such an extraordinary phenomenon and involving such a remarkable real person, the film is ultimately rather ordinary and unoriginal.
reviews.author: Christopher Campbell

reviews.text: An ode to gloriously terrible filmmaking, with Franco turning in perhaps his best performance to date.
reviews.author: Matthew Turner

reviews.text: An audacious high-wire act, a quirky tribute to outsiders everywhere and a celebration of a particularly bizarre moment in Hollywood-outsider footnote history.
reviews.author: Neil Pond

reviews.text: The Disaster Artist proves to be a hilarious and heartfelt tale of ambition, friendship, and the imponderable mind of creative force Tommy Wiseau, played here in astonishingly believable fashion by director James Franco.
reviews.author: Steve Newall

reviews.text: The Disaster Artist deserves to stand alongside Tim Burton's Ed Wood as an appreciation of someone whose creative enthusiasm somehow managed to shine through their total lack of talent.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: James Franco has placed enough links to the original film that his based-on-fact look at the making of The Room is weirdly fun on its own and one of the most creative films of the year.
reviews.author: Rick Bentley

reviews.text: James Franco's affectionate take on [The Room's] bizarre creation may yet end up at the Academy Awards.
reviews.author: Michele Manelis

reviews.text: [The Disaster Artist] is a wildly entertaining jaunt into the strange and wonderful world of independent filmmaking, and it's difficult to argue with that result.
reviews.author: Patrick Cooley

reviews.text: The result is a hysterical and loving tribute sure to generate just as much raucous cheering as one of The Room's urban midnight screenings.
reviews.author: Mara Reinstein

reviews.text: You could just look at this as one of the most seriously funny movies about movie making, but why stop there? Thanks to James Franco's canny eye, this love song to a film so bad it's good also delivers one of the best emotional surprises of the year.
reviews.author: Joanna Langfield

reviews.text: Whatever my queasiness about laughing at a head case, I couldn't help myself from thrilling to Franco's timing, his relish, his swan dive into an egotism that has no bottom.
reviews.author: David Edelstein

reviews.text: Director James Franco's enjoyable ode to the creative process - any creative process, really. It's also one of Franco's strongest roles as an actor, capturing every little quirk and quality of a definite eccentric.
reviews.author: Brian Truitt

reviews.text: James Franco has turned one of the worst movies ever made into a great one. That's not merely the result of hard graft, skill and luck. That's straight-up alchemy.
reviews.author: Simon Miraudo

reviews.text: The Disaster Artist, which Franco directed and stars in, has to be one of the best and sweetest and funniest films about failure I've ever seen.
reviews.author: Taylor Antrim

reviews.text: A sense of gnawing inadequacy is a universal feeling, and The Disaster Artist certainly mines the notion that there's a little bit of the outsider in everybody - which is exactly the kind of magnanimity you'd expect.
reviews.author: Bilge Ebiri

reviews.text: Painful, but it's positive, too. It's walking that line that takes The Disaster Artist beyond cringe comedy to an unexpectedly touching tribute to a 21st-century icon.
reviews.author: Rebecca Pahle

reviews.text: James Franco is firing on all his creative cylinders in this comic bonanza about Tommy Wiseau, the worst filmmaker of the 21st century. Franco hits a new career peak by making sure his film is as heartfelt as it is hilarious.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: For Franco, the opportunity to dramatize this prolonged agony of production is irresistible, and his wildly entertaining "The Disaster Artist" is a loving ode to the power of delusion.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: ... as actor Paul Scheer said at The Disaster Artist's Toronto Film Festival premiere, "it's the perfect prequel for those who've never seen The Room and the perfect sequel for those who have".
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: James Franco goes behind the scenes of The Room, a legend in its own right, and offers some of his best work yet in The Disaster Artist.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: A big reason why The Room is so effective is that there is but one, confirmed, solitary individual on that set that doesn't understand the burning building around him: Tommy himself. But in The Disaster Artist, that essential straight-man doesn't exist.
reviews.author: Leonardo Faierman

reviews.text: Oh hai, great movie! The Disaster Artist is a loving tribute to all those who dream big, even when everything seems to be going wrong.
reviews.author: Chris Stuckmann

reviews.text: This is an absolute crowd-pleaser that will have you laughing harder than most studio comedies.
reviews.author: Dan Barrett

reviews.text: James Franco directs the film with sensitivity and painstaking detail, and gives a fantastic performance as one of the worst filmmakers -- and one of the most unusual human beings -- ever.
reviews.author: William Bibbiani

reviews.text: Franco does not make fun of Wiseau, on the contrary, he seems to have a certain fascination with the character. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Aurélie Dupire

reviews.text: Know that you're in for a movie that flogs its fan service so vigorously (forget about a wink -- this is a squint), it barely remembers to be anything more than a mildly weird story of friendship and betrayal. Maybe that's all it needs to be.
reviews.author: Joshua Rothkopf

reviews.text: As a tagline for The Room once famously, falsely promised, The Disaster Artist burns with the passion of Tennessee Williams. As the subsequent tagline more honestly stated, experience this new black comedy; it's a riot.
reviews.author: Luke Y. Thompson

reviews.text: The hilarity and insanity will hook you, but the core of the film is male camaraderie and the indomitable spirit of an enigmatic 'auteur.'
reviews.author: Courtney Howard

reviews.text: A breezy and occasionally gut-busting story of a clueless, striving industry hopeful whose desire for success is in inverse proportion to the tools he possesses to achieve it.
reviews.author: Mark Keizer

reviews.text: The Disaster Artist exudes a more authentic understanding of the phenomenon. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Miguel Muñoz Garnica

reviews.text: Rather than simply turn Tommy into a laughing stock, Franco teases out the tragicomedy of the man.
reviews.author: Amber Wilkinson

reviews.text: Everything here depicting the making of Wiseau's magnum opus is detailed and hilarious.
reviews.author: Adam Nayman

reviews.text: It features a genially goofy (and accurate) impersonation of Wiseau by Franco himself, plus irresistible interplay between the actor-director and his brother Dave Franco as Sestero, making this a genuinely moving bromance in every sense.
reviews.author: Jonathan Romney

reviews.text: Franco remains one of the most fascinating performers of his generation, even if his directing ability needs a little work.
reviews.author: Brian Tallerico

reviews.text: What could have been a parody, evolves into a touching celebration of the man behind the worst movie ever made. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Orlando Maldonado

reviews.text: Inhabiting Wiseau's skin gives [James Franco] liberty to be as weird as he wants to be and it completely works. Even when Tommy's actions seem cruel, Franco's interpretation brims with sympathy.
reviews.author: Esther Zuckerman

reviews.text: The Disaster Artist comes off a lot like Ed Wood or even American Splendor, as it feels like there's always multiple layers to what Franco is doing.
reviews.author: Edward Douglas

reviews.text: Not just providing a one-note take on an enigmatic person, it captures unexpected layers that we never would have thought existed.
reviews.author: Jordan Ruimy

reviews.text: The Disaster Artist perfectly communicates the surreal hell of what the original production of The Room must have been like.
reviews.author: Jake Cole

reviews.text: The Disaster Artist is a love letter to movies and the people who dream big enough to make them, even when they have no clue what they're doing.
reviews.author: Sarah Marrs

reviews.text: A hilarious love-letter to Tommy Wiseau. You don't have to have seen THE ROOM to enjoy it, but you - ya know - should.
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: How did a story with this much potential get turned into something so unimaginative?
reviews.author: Ignatiy Vishnevetsky

reviews.text: The Disaster Artist makes a case for bad films everywhere by proving that some good (in this case great) can come from even the worst of them.
reviews.author: Jon Espino

reviews.text: James Franco pulls off what Tommy Wiseau only dreamed of.
reviews.author: Bryan Bishop

reviews.text: A triumphant story of friendship and a testament to the phrase 'go big or go home.'
reviews.author: Shane Slater

reviews.text: Franco's performance as Tommy Wiseau is a thing of beauty.
reviews.author: Matt Singer

reviews.text: The dazzle of the cast and the targeted in-jokes never take away from the film's core messaging about the importance of believing in one's own ability as an artist.
reviews.author: Benjamin Lee

reviews.text: Franco takes what could have easily been a parody and make Wiseau into a real, three-dimensional person who not only makes us laugh with all of his eccentricities, but also gets us to care about his loneliness and insecurities.
reviews.author: Matt Goldberg

reviews.text: I'm not saying "The Disaster Artist" is the best movie you'll see this year, but it's certainly the most fun.
reviews.author: Jason Guerrasio

reviews.text: The Disaster Artist is just a total delight.
reviews.author: Mike Ryan

reviews.text: A shockingly poignant portrait of the jealousies that arise when the creative process goes haywire.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: Whether or not you actually like The Room is irrelevant; The Disaster Artist is its own giddy thing, and you don't have to force yourself to laugh.
reviews.author: Norman Wilner

reviews.text: Franco brings his A game to this project and puts his heart and soul into the material.
reviews.author: Scott Menzel

reviews.text: Franco wants to have his cake and eat it too, openly mocking Wiseau for his weirdness, then heralding him for his persistence and ability to embrace The Room's reputation.
reviews.author: Kristy Puchko

reviews.text: Conversely, The Disaster Artist - a new film about the making of The Room - is not only the rare example of a genuinely funny biopic, but a subtle meta-commentary on the state of cult filmmaking.
reviews.author: Adi Robertson

reviews.text: Gives you context to start and really makes you feel like you've seen the best parts of The Room, although I'm told it's all great.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: Miraculously, the supporting players end up illuminating Wiseau's eccentricity instead of undercutting it.
reviews.author: Sam Fragoso

reviews.text: Nothing this great has ever come from something so bad. A career-best performance from James Franco.
reviews.author: Nathan McVay

reviews.text: The Disaster artist is obscurest hilarity set to a filmmaker's struggle, all linked to James Franco's transformative performance as the mythical Tommy Wiseau.
reviews.author: Matt Donato

reviews.text: It's James Franco's best performance since his Oscar-nominated turn in "127 Hours" and as a director it is nice to finally seem him embrace the comfort zone of comedy with enough cameos to rival Robert Altman's "The Player."
reviews.author: Erik Childress

reviews.text: It's a hilarious master class in self-referentiality, as well as an affectionate and reverential tribute to Tommy Wiseau and his mad creation.
reviews.author: Marten Carlson

reviews.text: It may soon join Tim Burton's Ed Wood in the ranks of great movies about terrible movies.
reviews.author: Jada Yuan

reviews.text: The Disaster Artist largely works because it brings us closer to Tommy while reveling in the same ingredients that have turned him into an icon.
reviews.author: Ben Travers

reviews.text: [Boasts] a genuine capacity to delight, whether or not the audiences in question have seen "The Room."
reviews.author: Peter Debruge

reviews.text: Strikes a giddy, winning balance between hilarity and heart.
reviews.author: Michael Rechtshaffen

synopsis: The incredible true story of aspiring filmmaker and Hollywood outsider Tommy Wiseau as he and his best friend defiantly pursue their dreams and embark on the hilarious odyssey of making the now-infamous, cult classic "The Room."
